note: Governor's veto message titles the bill "An Act to Establish the Maine Data Center Coordination Council and Place a Temporary Limitation on Certain Data Centers". The repository holds the pre-amendment committee title ("An Act Regarding Energy, Utilities And Technology"), which is why the subject gate could not see it. As amended it placed a moratorium on permitting data centers of 20 MW or more until 2027-11-01. Passed both chambers, vetoed, veto sustained.

note: Utility RELIEF Act, signed 2026-05-12. Requires large load customers including data centers to register with the Public Service Commission and to pay for their own grid upgrades, and lowers the large-load rate-schedule threshold from 100 MW to 25 MW. PARTIAL: an omnibus energy affordability act covering net metering, grid planning and utility regulation, so a vote on it is not a position on its data center provisions. No direction asserted.

note: Certified Microgrid Program. Creates certification for "microgrid districts" and "high impact data centers" (90 MW or more), streamlines their development, grants regulatory exemptions inside districts and sets a special property tax valuation and tax distribution framework for high impact data centers. Enabling: it grants and accelerates rather than constrains.

note: Amends the Municipalities Planning Code to let a municipality adopt a resolution pausing review of new data center land development applications for up to 180 days. Passed the House 201-1 on 2026-06-24. Restrictive: it creates local authority to halt applications.

note: Reference title "utilities; high load factor customers", signed 2026-06-04. Directs the Corporation Commission to adopt rules for extra high load factor customers (data centers), including pre-execution contract review in the interest of other ratepayers, cost-of-service studies and semiannual interconnection reporting. Restrictive: cost allocation and contract conditions. NOTE the subject lexicon deliberately does not carry "high load factor" -- it is a general utility rate-class term that also covers steel mills, so this bill is promoted by citation rather than by widening the gate.

note: Extends the Enterprise Zone property tax exemption from five to ten years and, by the Nathanson amendment, makes new data centers ineligible for the expanded benefit until 90 days after the 2027 session adjourns. Effective 2026-06-05. PARTIAL: the vehicle is an enterprise zone extension and the data center moratorium is a carve-out inside it, so a yes vote cannot be read as a position on the carve-out. No direction asserted.

note: Ratepayer Protection Act. Applies to data centers of 100 MW or more: closed-loop cooling, 15-year minimum utility contracts, minimum billing, responsibility for grid and generation costs, environmental and noise review, and a bar on eminent domain and local incentives. Passed the House 69-44. PARTIAL: the same bill reshapes long-range power planning and carries fossil and nuclear provisions that drew their own opposition, so a no vote may be about those rather than the data center title. No direction asserted.

note: Land use and development. Would make large developments including data centers a permitted use on lower-grade agricultural land, bypassing local zoning and public hearings, and require new data centers to share at least 1 percent of their sales tax savings with local government. Passed the House 54-45; stalled in Senate Utilities. PARTIAL: a general land use bill that also covers solar, so a vote on it is not a position on its data center provisions. No direction asserted.
